title: International Payment Gateway vs Wire Transfer: Which Fits Your Export Sale?
summary: Compare international payment gateways, wire transfers and local bank collections for export sales. Check fees, settlement, invoice limits and payment documents.
body_markdown:
Table of Contents


Toggle


Every export sale ends with the same question: how will the money reach your Indian bank account? For many Indian businesses, the answer comes down to two common international payment collection methods. You can collect through an international payment gateway, where the buyer pays by card, PayPal or Apple Pay at checkout. Or you can collect through a bank transfer, where the buyer sends money from their bank account to yours.


Both are reliable ways of receiving export payments in India, but they suit different buyers, different invoice sizes and different ways of selling. This guide compares an international payment gateway vs wire transfer, while also distinguishing local bank collection rails, so you can match each export sale to the method that fits it best.


### Key Takeaways


- Gateways suit checkout-led purchases; bank transfers often suit invoice-led business payments.
- A direct SWIFT wire and a local collection payment through ACH or SEPA are different routes.
- Compare the net INR received after processing charges, bank deductions, FX and applicable taxes.
- Confirm product limits, settlement timing and remittance documents for the chosen route. A payment receipt does not complete every export reporting requirement.


##


What Are Export Payments and Collection Methods?


When a buyer in another country sends money to an Indian merchant, the money entering the merchant’s account is called a foreign inward remittance. The foreign inward remittance may involve selling handmade items to a Canadian customer, providing software to German companies, or delivering consulting services to clients in Singapore. These are all forms of transferring money from outside India into India.


Each of these transfers involves documentation as well as crossing boundaries. Therefore, exporters require proof that the money transferred into India originated from a foreign source and was used for buying products or providing services. This proof includes a foreign inward remittance statement (FIRS), or foreign inward remittance advice (e-FIRA). Both[FIRS and e-FIRA](https://www.cashfree.com/blog/firc/) are explained below. To summarize, it is important to remember that the method of payment chosen by the exporter will affect how quickly the exporter receives these documents as much as how quickly the exporter receives the money.


Cash in advance, open account, documentary collection and letters of credit describe commercial payment terms and arrangements. This article compares collection channels, which you should choose alongside those terms.


##


How Does an International Payment Gateway Work for Exports?


A payment gateway facilitates international online purchases by allowing buyers who reside in other countries to make an online purchase from merchants located inside India. At the moment of check-out when the consumer chooses their preferred payment option, the consumer enters their personal and financial information. The consumer may be able to pay in their own currency at the time of completing the transaction, depending on the supported checkout and payment method. Following the successful transaction, the provider and its banking partners handle the applicable conversion and settlement to your registered Indian bank account. Payment confirmation and bank settlement are separate events.


With our International Payment Gateway, your customers can choose from the following payment options:


- **International cards:** 140+ currencies accepted; Visa, Mastercard, American Express, Maestro
- **Apple Pay:** One touch purchase available to[Apple Pay](https://www.cashfree.com/blog/apple-pay-in-india/) users in USA, UK, UAE, Canada, Australia etc.
- **PayPal:** Consumer can pay using PayPal directly via Cashfree checkout
- **Local bank transfers:** Local collection accounts are another Cashfree collection option, discussed separately below. They should not be confused with card or wallet checkout.


Depending on the type of payment selected by the consumer you are allowed to receive international payments from consumers across over 170 countries. International card payments typically settle to your registered Indian bank account in rupees within T+2 business days, subject to the agreed terms. Confirm settlement separately for PayPal and other methods. A FIRS (foreign inward remittance statement) report will automatically be created for each international payment made. Using your dashboard, you are able to view FIRS reports; confirm their availability and reporting schedule for the payment method.


Additionally, there are some tools and features that can assist in streamlining the process of selling internationally. For example, you can offer consumers international subscriptions using[recurring payments](https://www.cashfree.com/recurring-payment/) utilizing tiered pricing, usage-based pricing, one-time pricing or free trial pricing. Also, you can show prices to consumers in their local currency to build confidence in purchasing and reduce the abandonment rate associated with paying internationally. Depending on the payment flow and enabled features, Cashfree supports 3D Secure 2.0,[RiskShield](https://www.cashfree.com/risk-shield-payment-gateway/) and address verification for supported US and Canadian card transactions. These controls support fraud management; approval remains subject to issuer decisions.


##


How Do Wire Transfers and Local Bank Collections Work?


Historically, Indian exporters were paid through bank transfers. The exporter shares their banking details on the invoice. The importer sends the funds from their bank account. This type of payment is known as an[international wire transfer](https://www.cashfree.com/blog/swift-money-transfer/) . Many international wires use[SWIFT’s secure messaging network](https://www.swift.com/about-us/who-we-are) for payment instructions; the actual funds move through banks and other financial institutions.


However, there is a much easier way to receive bank transfers from outside India. Using Cashfree Global Collections, eligible businesses can get dedicated local collection account details across 4 currencies (USD, GBP, EUR & CAD), plus a Global SWIFT Account to accept payments in 30+ currencies from 180+ countries.


Using a local account for your buyers to send funds creates a different experience for them. They do not need to send an international wire. They simply pay through their country’s respective payment networks similar to how they would pay a local vendor:


- ACH (Automated Clearing House) in USA
- SEPA (Single Euro Payments Area) in Europe
- EFT (Electronic Fund Transfer) in Canada
- Faster Payments in United Kingdom


For example, a buyer in the US can make a payment to your local USD account via ACH transfer. You do not need to establish a bank account overseas. Once the buyer makes a deposit into your local account, we settle those funds into your INR-denominated bank account in India. We generate an e-FIRA (foreign inward remittance advice) automatically within 24 hours at no extra charge to you.


Before you begin using Global Collections, here are some points about its limitations:


- Each individual transaction amount may not exceed $10,000.
- There is no maximum on the number of transactions processed daily/weekly/monthly.
- All settlements occur exclusively in INR-denominated amounts.
- Settlement occurs no later than 7 days post-credit entry to our NOSTRO collection account.
- High value goods (such as jewelry), petroleum products/oils/lubricants, pharmaceuticals/equipment are excluded from eligibility for this service.


The[RBI PA Directions](https://www.rbi.org.in/Scripts/BS_ViewMasDirections.aspx?id=12896) set a ₹25 lakh maximum per inward or outward PA-CB transaction and require transparent settlement timelines in the merchant agreement. This regulatory ceiling is separate from a provider’s product eligibility or transaction limit.


##


Which Export Payment Method Fits Your Sale?


The best solution to use depends on which party you have making the payment, the preference of that party regarding how they would like to make the payment and the size of the invoice. Below is how to connect the method with the sale.


Consideration International payment gateway Direct international wire Local bank collection through a provider


Buyer action Pays at checkout using an enabled card or wallet Instructs their bank to remit to your bank Pays local collection details using an eligible rail such as ACH or SEPA


Typical fit Online consumer orders and supported subscriptions Invoice-led business payments, including eligible larger invoices Invoice-led payments within the product’s supported scope


Cost to compare Processing fee, FX, taxes, refunds and disputes Sender, intermediary and recipient fees, plus FX Collection fee, FX and any settlement or return charges


Timing to confirm Checkout result and settlement cycle Bank processing, checks and final beneficiary credit Local-rail processing, verification and settlement to India


Documentation Provider/bank remittance records plus export documents Bank receipt/advice plus export documents Provider/bank remittance records plus export documents


### You Sell Physical Products Online


You sell physical products over the internet to consumers outside your country. An international payment gateway is often a suitable choice. Consumers purchasing goods over the web, especially those purchasing internationally, typically want to pay via credit cards, Apple Pay or PayPal upon check out, not via bank transfer. Cashfree can collect shipping information and provide FIRS records for international payments. You still need the applicable shipping, invoice and customs records; a FIRS is not shipment clearance.


### You Sell Digital Products


You sell digital products. Then consider an international payment gateway. If you are selling software, courses or downloads, customers wish to obtain instant access to their purchased items. Therefore, a gateway can provide a checkout suited to digital delivery. Required buyer, billing and compliance information still depends on the transaction; digital goods are not automatically free of export documentation requirements.


### You Sell Retainers or Subscriptions


You sell services on a retainer or subscription basis. Then consider an international payment gateway for supported recurring collections, or a bank transfer for agreed invoice-based payments. You can charge clients either by issuing one-time invoices or billing them via recurring retainers utilizing a single integration. Cashfree advertises international recurring billing in 140+ currencies; confirm method availability, customer authorisation and the integration required for your plan.


### You Invoice Importers or Other Business Buyers


You generate invoices to importers or other commercial buyers. Then consider a bank transfer through Global Collections, if each invoice falls within the published USD 10,000 product limit and the other eligibility requirements. Many business buyers prefer to purchase supplies from suppliers in their country via a bank transfer. As they pay suppliers locally, a local account enables them to pay you similarly.


### Your Invoice Falls Outside the Collection Product’s Scope


Your invoice exceeds $10,000 or you are generating an invoice for a product excluded from Global Collections. In that event, the published Global Collections offering may not be suitable for this sale. For a lawful export outside its product scope, discuss a direct bank wire into your Indian bank account or another eligible route with your AD bank.


##


Cross-Border Payment Fees Comparison: What to Include


In many cases, fees will determine whether a customer chooses a particular provider or service. Thus, comparing the total charges associated with all of your possible international payment collection options (not simply the stated rate) will help.


**An international payment gateway:** The regular published standard rate on Cashfree for each successful international card transaction is 2.99%, with no initial fee for setup. Large volume companies can get custom enterprise pricing. FX is applied on the settlement amount. Check the conversion rate, applicable GST and any additional charges in the written quote.


**PayPal via the gateway:** Transactions processed via PayPal are charged according to PayPal’s rates and applicable agreement. Compare PayPal’s processing and conversion costs separately; the gateway’s standard international card rate should not be assumed to apply.


**Bank transfer via Global Collections:** Cashfree lists no subscription fees and no forex markup. You pay under the applicable collection pricing. Its advertised savings of up to 50% compared to conventional bank transfers depend on the bank charges, payment corridor and quote used for comparison.


For a cross-border payment fees comparison using the[applicable pricing](https://www.cashfree.com/payment-gateway-charges/) , ask the following questions relative to each option:


- What percentage or fixed fee do I incur on each transaction?
- Is there a markup on the foreign exchange rate used?
- Are there any fees for setting up, maintaining or renewing my account?
- How much of the money I collect ends up in my Indian rupee (INR) bank account?


As a simple processing-fee illustration, 2.99% of a payment value equivalent to ₹1,00,000 is ₹2,990 before applicable taxes, FX and other charges. Compare that with the complete bank-transfer quote for the same invoice and currency; a lower headline fee does not establish a higher net INR receipt.


For a direct wire, ask who bears sending-bank, intermediary and receiving-bank charges. Also compare refund or return costs and the time until the funds are usable.


##


Receiving Export Payments in India: FIRS, e-FIRA and eBRC


A FIRS (foreign inward remittance statement) records an international payment received in India. It can support reconciliation and compliance, but the document required depends on your AD bank, transaction and the scheme or tax purpose. FIRS, e-FIRA and eBRC are not interchangeable, and no single remittance record automatically establishes GST or export-incentive eligibility.


Below is how each Cashfree method addresses this paperwork.


**International Payment Gateway:** For every eligible international payment made via Cashfree, a FIRS is generated and available for download from your dashboard as a report.


**Global Collections:** Cashfree advertises automatic e-FIRA generation within 24 hours at no extra cost. Confirm the document type, issuer, delivery timing and available payment references for your route.


Keep your invoice,[purpose code](https://www.cashfree.com/blog/purpose-code-for-international-payments/) , remittance references and net bank credit aligned for[settlement reconciliation](https://www.cashfree.com/settlement-and-reconciliation-guide/) . Under DGFT’s eBRC process, exporters self-generate eBRCs using bank-reported IRMs where applicable. eBRC generation and bank-side EDPMS reconciliation are separate processes.


##


Can You Use Both International Payment Collection Methods?


Yes. Your company sells merchandise to retail customers around the world and possibly sends invoices to some overseas distributors. In this instance, you may utilize the gateway for processing online sales and Global Collections for invoicing business accounts.


Both solutions are offered by Cashfree. Cashfree has[RBI authorisation as a Payment Aggregator for Cross Border Payments (PA-CB)](https://www.cashfree.com/international-payment-gateway/) , for both exports and imports. Product-specific limits and eligibility still apply.

3. Share the account details with your international clients.
4. Track your transactions and obtain your e-FIRA (foreign inward remittance advice).

##


FAQs


#### 1. What is the primary difference between an international payment gateway and a wire transfer?


An international payment gateway allows buyers to make purchases online by entering their payment information during check-out via card, Apple Pay or PayPal. A wire transfer is when a buyer sends money from their bank account to your bank account via a direct bank-to-bank transfer.


#### 2. Which global payment method is most economical?


It depends on how you market and sell. The Cashfree International Payment Gateway charges 2.99% per successful transaction as standard for card payments. Cashfree Global Collections lists no subscription fees and no forex markup. Compare the full quote against bank transfer charges, FX and the amount you will actually receive; no method is always the cheapest.


#### 3. Can I accept export payments greater than USD 10,000 through Global Collections?


Cashfree’s published Global Collections FAQ currently describes eligibility up to USD 10,000 per transaction. Confirm the current route and limit during onboarding before accepting a larger invoice. The PA-CB regulatory ceiling does not mean that every product supports transactions up to that ceiling.


#### 4. When do I expect to receive my international payments in India?


International card payments through the Cashfree International Payment Gateway typically settle in INR within T+2 business days, subject to the agreed terms. For Global Collections and other payment methods, confirm the route-specific settlement cycle, verification conditions and cut-offs in your agreement.


#### 5. Do I require a foreign bank account to receive payments in USD, EUR, GBP or CAD?


No. Cashfree Global Collections provides local collection account details in each of those currencies, enabling you to receive payments without opening your own overseas bank account. Settlement for this offering is to your Indian bank account in INR.


#### 6. Can I retain international payments in foreign currency?


The published Global Collections offering settles to your Indian bank account in INR. Other permitted foreign-currency arrangements may be available through eligible providers or your AD bank; confirm the supported setup before planning to retain foreign currency.
